newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends slightly up in dull market.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends slightly up in dull market.

text.p: * Market resting amidst lack of fresh incentives
The Philippine peso ended a shade higher in narrow-range trading on Wednesday at 26.227 pesos to the dollar from 26.228, traders said.
The day's average was also at 26.227 versus the previous day's 26.229. Volume thinned to $82.70 million from $105.0 million.
"Market was in equilibrium. Portfolio investments were just enough to offset demand," said a trader from a big bank.
Another trader said the market was just resting after building up positions last week in anticipation of the higher demand for dollars in case U.S. interest rates are raised next week.

The trader added the long dollar positions of some banks are now justified in view of Tuesday's report by the Asian Development Bank expressing concern that the appreciating trend of the peso could put further pressure on the country's trade balance.
Traders said they are awaiting cues from the Central Bank before aggressively positioning again. The Central Bank has kept away from the foreign exchange market for two days now.
